sections.title: Bracket and tag matching
sections.intro: When the caret is on a bracket or a tag name, the editor marks it and its partner. These classes come from the matching extensions rather than from the syntax highlighting, so they sit outside the wikitext theme and are the same in every mode. VisualEditor's source mode cannot draw them, because the Custom Highlight API has no outline. In the examples below the caret is just after the opening bracket or tag name.

sections.title: Nesting
sections.intro: Every token inside a template, extension tag or link also carries a "ground" class recording how deeply it is nested. They tint the background so nested structures stay legible, and they combine: a template inside a template inside a link is cm-mw-template2-link-ground. Nesting is counted up to three levels. cm-mw-template-ground has no tint of its own, so a single unnested template is not shaded.

notes.visualEditor: The swatches are drawn with the editor's own style sheets, which this page turns off for VisualEditor source mode. The tints themselves do apply there, on the text: you can see them in the nested examples above.
notes.noTints: This theme removes the nesting tints, so every swatch is blank.

sections.title: Extension and tag names
sections.intro: Each parser tag the wiki has installed gets a cm-mw-ext-<name> class on the tag itself. Tags whose content the editor tokenizes, such as nowiki, pre and ref, also put cm-mw-tag-<name> on that content. Which tags exist depends on the extensions installed, so the list below is from a typical Wikimedia wiki rather than yours. Only nowiki, pre and templatestyles are styled by default; the rest are hooks for your own CSS.
